question: With a fixed corpus but effectively unlimited training compute, which combination of repetition, regularization, model scaling, ensembling, and distillation minimizes held-out language-model loss?

key_findings.claim: Naively increasing either epochs or model parameters eventually overfits the 200M-token corpus.
key_findings.evidence: After tuning epoch count and learning rate, loss stops improving and the 1.4B model is worse than the 600M model; excessive repetition also reverses the loss gain.

key_findings.claim: Jointly tuning weight decay, learning rate and epochs restores monotone parameter scaling, with the largest models preferring weight decay more than 30 times the common 0.1 setting.
key_findings.evidence: The regularized recipe follows an approximately inverse-parameter excess-loss law up to parameter-to-token ratios 140 times Chinchilla and yields an estimated 3.43 infinite-parameter asymptote.

key_findings.claim: Independent logit ensembles have a lower fitted asymptote than single-model parameter scaling, and hyperparameters optimal for one member are not optimal for an infinite ensemble.
key_findings.evidence: At 300M parameters per member, the fitted ensemble asymptote improves from 3.34 to 3.27 after ensemble-specific tuning, versus 3.43 for the regularized single-model limit.

key_findings.claim: Distilling an eight-member ensemble into a 300M student retains 83% of the ensemble improvement, while the composed recipe is estimated to use 5.17 times less seed data at the 200M-token asymptote.
key_findings.evidence: The student is eight times smaller than the combined teacher ensemble; downstream pretraining benchmarks improve by 9% on average, and math continued pretraining is reported as 17.5 times more data efficient.

method.core_idea: Replace finite-compute model selection by comparing fitted loss asymptotes under a fixed-data, no-compute-constraint objective.
method.mechanism: Train Llama-style models on a controlled DCLM subset, tune regularization and epoch count at each scale, fit parameter- and ensemble-count power laws with floors, compose the limits, and recover inference efficiency through distillation.
assumptions: Held-out i.i.d. loss is the objective and predicts downstream utility at the studied scale.
Power-law fits from finite model and ensemble grids extrapolate meaningfully to infinite scale.
The 200M-token controlled regime and its data-scaling fits transfer to much larger pretraining corpora.

techniques.role: Ranks algorithms by fitted loss floors instead of a fixed compute budget.
Coordinates weight decay, learning rate, epoch count, and parameter count under data scarcity.
Uses independent-model diversity for a lower loss limit and compresses it into one student.

evaluations.setting: Llama-style models from 150M to 1.4B parameters trained repeatedly on 200M DCLM tokens.
evaluations.metric: Validation cross-entropy and fitted scaling-law asymptote.
evaluations.result: Naive scaling overfits; tuned regularization is monotone, and ensemble scaling reaches a lower fitted floor.
evaluations.baseline: Repeated-data standard recipe and single regularized model scaling.

evaluations.setting: Distillation, ARC-Easy/PIQA/SciQ, and MegaMath-Web-Pro continued pretraining.
evaluations.metric: Retained loss gain, benchmark error, and data needed to match a baseline.
evaluations.result: The 300M student retains 83% of the eight-model gain; reported downstream and math-data efficiencies improve.
evaluations.baseline: Best single regularized model and default continued-pretraining recipe.

limitations: The headline is based on extrapolated asymptotes rather than training at anything close to infinite compute.
Most controlled experiments use only 200M unique tokens and sub-2B models.
Ensembling incurs large training and serving cost unless distillation succeeds, and student results cover a narrow scale.
Validation and downstream comparisons do not address memorization, privacy, or distribution shift under heavy repetition.
failure_modes: A misspecified power-law floor can reverse the ranking of recipes outside the observed range.
Large weight decay can underfit richer or changing corpora.
Ensemble members may become too correlated for the projected diversity gain, especially with deterministic data order or initialization.
reusable_insights: Data-constrained scaling requires retuning regularization rather than reusing compute-optimal defaults.
Algorithm comparisons under a relaxed resource constraint need an explicit limiting objective and extrapolation audit.
Distillation can separate an expensive training-time diversity mechanism from inference-time model size.
open_questions: Do the fitted asymptote rankings survive at trillion-token and tens-of-billions-parameter scale?
Can explicit diversity objectives beat independent ensembles at the same total training FLOPs?
What contamination and memorization signals appear after the high epoch counts selected by the recipe?

competitive_landscape.title: Scaling Data-Constrained Language Models
competitive_landscape.relationship: Closest predecessor on repeated-data scaling under corpus scarcity.
competitive_landscape.difference: Muennighoff et al. model diminishing returns at fixed compute and report little penalty through roughly four epochs; the target removes the compute constraint, exposes eventual overfit, and retunes regularization and ensembles.

competitive_landscape.title: Training Compute-Optimal Large Language Models
competitive_landscape.difference: Chinchilla allocates a finite compute budget between fresh data and parameters; the target fixes unique data and studies the opposite limiting regime where additional compute is free.

competitive_landscape.title: Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models
competitive_landscape.difference: Kaplan et al. fit finite-resource language-model loss laws with effectively fresh data; the target uses floor-bearing laws to compare data-reuse algorithms as compute tends to infinity.

novelty_assessment: The paper's useful novelty is treating fixed-data pretraining recipes as asymptotic algorithms and showing that strong regularization plus ensemble diversity changes the estimated floor. The infinite-compute wording must remain visibly extrapolative, and prior data-constrained and compute-optimal laws already define the surrounding problem.
reviewer_notes: Read all 45 extracted pages, including hyperparameter searches, scaling fits, distillation, downstream checks, and sensitivity appendices. Primary arXiv competitor records were checked on 2026-08-23.
